And with that most of my previous relationships stem from the guys I am dating on really dating me because of my looks and the "status symbol" of dating a model not because of me as a person. This is something that has caused a lot of anxiety and depression in my life and I have been really trying to find people in my life that care about me not what I look like. Now that is not to say that my looks can't play a role (physical attraction is important to me as well) but I can't be with anyone where that is the only or main reason why they are dating me. So that brings me to a guy a started dating fairly recently. I really like him and he seems like a good guy. Takes interest in my hobbies and is supportive of what I do. He enjoys lazy days around the house and cooking for me at home instead of always wanting to go out (which with a lot of guys it just seemed like they wanted to show me off). So I really really like him. But his friend DM'd me the other day and told me, "Hey, just thought you should know. You boyfriend has been telling anyone who will listen about all the dirty shit he gets to do with 'this model chick I have been banging'. I'd want to know. Hope for the best!" I have only met this guy once and I don't know how close he is to my boyfriend nor do I know why he told me this. For all I know he is just trying to start drama. The problem is I know how badly I want to believe my boyfriend. And if he were to tell me that it isn't true I would probably believe him. But that thought of "what if" would constantly be in my head from now on. So would I be an asshole if for the next month or so I stop wearing makeup when we go out and I don't put out at all (just come up with whatever excuse I need to when he starts trying to make a move)? If I test what his motives truly are? Part of me feels like this is wrong but the other part knows this is the only way I can fully 100% put this behind me. And if his friend is lying I can commit to him 100%

Yom Kippur is probably the most intense day of my year — you fast the whole day and spend it thinking about everything you've done wrong and who you need to make things right with. Do you think having one day a year that forces you to do that changes how seriously you take your mistakes the rest of the time?

Yom Kippur serves as a significant catalyst for personal growth and mindfulness, offering a structured time for reflection and accountability. Here's how it can influence one's approach to mistakes and personal growth throughout the year: 1. **Focus and Introspection**: The day provides a break from routine, allowing deep reflection on actions and relationships, leading to clearer insights and a stronger resolve to change. 2. **Accountability**: Knowing there's a day dedicated to reflection can make individuals more mindful of their actions, fostering accountability and consciousness of their behavior. 3. **Community and Tradition**: As a communal practice, Yom Kippur reinforces the importance of reflection and amends, creating a supportive environment that encourages positive change. 4. **Habit Formation**: The day can inspire habits of regular self-reflection and self-improvement, leading to a consistent approach to addressing mistakes and personal growth. 5. **Forgiveness and Renewal**: The act of seeking forgiveness and making amends can provide a sense of renewal, motivating individuals to maintain better relationships and mindful actions. The effectiveness of Yom Kippur depends on how individuals integrate its lessons into daily life. If approached with genuine commitment, it can be transformative, fostering a mindful and intentional approach to actions and relationships throughout the year. Thus, Yom Kippur can indeed change how seriously people take their mistakes, encouraging a more thoughtful and proactive stance in their lives.

What do you personally think about this — is it right or wrong, and why?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out what to do in this situation. I'm a model, and most of my past relationships have been with guys who were more interested in my looks and the status of dating a model rather than me as a person. This has caused me a lot of anxiety and depression, and I really want to find someone who cares about me for who I am, not just my looks. That's not to say that physical attraction isn't important to me, but I can't be with someone where that's the only or main reason they're dating me. Now, I'm dating this guy who seems really good. He takes interest in my hobbies, supports what I do, and likes lazy days at home, cooking for me instead of always wanting to go out, which is different from a lot of other guys I've been with. I really like him, but there's this issue that came up recently. His friend DM'd me and told me that my boyfriend has been telling anyone who'll listen about all the "dirty shit" he gets to do with 'this model chick I've been banging.' The friend said they just thought I should know and hoped for the best. I've only met this guy once, and I don't know how close he is to my boyfriend or why he told me this. For all I know, he's just trying to start drama. But the problem is, I know how badly I want to believe my boyfriend. If he were to tell me it's not true, I would probably believe him. But that thought of "what if" would constantly be in my head from now on. So, would I be an asshole if, for the next month or so, I stop wearing makeup when we go out and don't put out at all (just come up with whatever excuse I need when he starts trying to make a move)? If I test what his motives truly are? Part of me feels like this is wrong, but the other part knows this is the only way I can fully, 100%, put this behind me. And if his friend is lying, I can commit to him 100%. I'm really confused about whether this is the right approach or not. On one hand, I want to protect myself and make sure I'm not getting hurt again, but on the other hand, I don't want to push my boyfriend away or make him feel like I don't trust him. I also don't want to ruin a good relationship if it's genuine. Maybe I should talk to him about it directly instead of testing him. But what if he gets defensive or thinks I don't trust him? I don't want to create unnecessary tension. But at the same time, I need to know for sure so I can move forward without the lingering doubt. I guess another option is to give him the benefit of the doubt and see how things go, but that leaves me with the anxiety of wondering if his friend was telling the truth. It's a tough spot to be in because I value trust in a relationship, and I don't want to be in a situation where I'm constantly doubting my partner. Perhaps I should also consider talking to a friend or a therapist about this to get an outside perspective. They might have some advice on how to handle this situation in a way that's fair to both me and my boyfriend. Overall, I'm really torn between wanting to protect myself and wanting to trust my boyfriend. I need to find a balance where I can feel secure in the relationship without feeling like I'm walking on eggshells.
